title: CUDA kernel optimization notes: FlashAttention, fused ops, paged KV
content:
Summary:

This is a working note collecting thoughts/experiments for CUDA kernel-level optimizations we want to evaluate for the serving runtime. Focus areas: FlashAttention integration and tuning, operator fusion opportunities (attention+softmax, qkv matmul+proj+dropout, rotary fusions), and an approach for paged KV cache that minimizes GPU memory pressure while preserving low latency for common prefixes. This is intentionally informal — experimental plans, microbench ideas, and open questions are included.

Goals / success criteria:
- Reduce per-token GPU time by ~15-30% for medium-length sequences (512–2048) on A100/H100-like hardware.
- Enable batch sizes up to our Dedicated targets without exceeding memory SLOs.
- Provide a paged KV cache fallback that keeps steady latency for hot prefixes while allowing very long-context corpora to be supported via CPU-backed pages.
- Keep changes modular: enable/disable fused kernels at runtime and fall back to reference kernels for correctness/debug.

Constraints and considerations:
- Must be compatible with mixed-precision (fp16/ bf16) and quantized int8 paths; kernel paths should accept both where possible.
- Interoperate with existing runtime tiling/batching so we don’t force a full rewrite of the operator graph.
- Safety/correctness > perf for canary rollouts — we need test harnesses that validate numerical parity within epsilon for fp16 paths.
- Maintainability: prefer fused kernels that are reusable across model families (gpt-like, bloomy-style, LLaMA variants).

FlashAttention recap (where we stand):
- FlashAttention reduces memory traffic by computing attention with a streaming algorithm that avoids explicit large softmax matrices. It shines for long sequences because it avoids O(L^2) memory.
- For serving, the typical pattern is autoregressive decode where we incrementally append tokens; FlashAttention v2 provides efficient causal kernels optimized for single-step incremental decoding using cached KV.
- Implementation note: FlashAttention requires careful workspace allocation and uses warp-level primitives; integration into our runtime must coordinate allocator and stream semantics.

Open implementation questions for FlashAttention in our runtime:
- Kernel selection policy: pick FlashAttention for full-attention patterns when sequence length > threshold (tunable). Lower lengths may be faster with small matmuls + softmax.
- Workspace lifetime: whether to reuse per-request workspace across batches to avoid frequent cudaMalloc/cudaFree. Likely we need a per-GPU pool keyed by workspace size.
- Backward compatibility: when using quantized kernels (INT8/4-bit), FlashAttention may not be available; runtime must fall back to non-flash path.

Fused ops ideas (prioritized):
1) qkv matmul -> split -> bias -> reshape -> rotary -> attention dot-product chain
  - Combine the projection matmul and qkv bias add + transpose into a single kernel that outputs packed Q/K/V in the layout optimal for subsequent attention kernel (e.g., interleaved).
  - Benefit: reduce memory writes/reads and eliminate an intermediate buffer copy + reshape.
  - Risks: complexity across model dims, need to support variable head counts and hidden_sizes.
2) fusing softmax + dropout + scale into a single kernel for attention weights
  - Common pattern: softmax over scaled scores, dropout mask application, then matmul with V. Fusing reduces memory traffic by keeping softmax outputs in registers and immediately applying dropout.
  - For deterministic runs (inference typically no dropout) fusion is simpler; for eval/training emulation we must keep RNG semantics.
3) rotary embedding fusion applied inside Q/K packing kernel
  - Apply rotary transformations during qkv pack so we avoid separate kernel pass.
4) final projection + residual + layernorm fusion (when using pre/post-layernorm variants)
  - Fusegemm with bias + residual add followed by approximate/fused rmsnorm where possible.

Paged KV cache design (notes + draft spec):
- Problem: long-context retrieval and multi-document chat can cause KV cache to exceed GPU memory quickly. Holding entire KV for every concurrent request is not feasible for Dedicated customers with heavy concurrency.

Design goals:
- Keep low-latency access for recent/hot prefixes (last N tokens) on GPU.
- Keep cold/rare prefixes paged out to CPU (or NVMe) and only brought to GPU on demand with async prefetch.
- Support eviction/replication policies that favor per-customer QoS (e.g., VIP customers pinned to GPU memory).

High-level architecture:
- Per-request KV logical address space divided into fixed-size pages (page size tunable, default 256 or 512 token-worth).
- Each page can be resident on GPU or CPU. GPU-resident pages have fast device pointers; CPU pages live in pinned host memory for fast cudaMemcpy if needed.
- Read path for decode: if required page is resident on GPU -> direct device read; else: enqueue async copy (cpu->gpu) and optionally schedule small micro-batch reordering to hide copy latency.
- Prefetch policy: when decode penetrates into a cold page, prefetch next M pages (heuristic) and re-order upcoming requests to decode other requests that are already resident.

Eviction and memory accounting:
- LRU-ish policy per-GPU with per-customer weights. Eviction triggers a thin serialization to CPU pinned buffer. For customers with dedicated pools, honor pin directives.
- Memory accounting must include workspace and fused-kernel scratch buffers (FlashAttention workspaces) to avoid OOM from workspace spikes.

Interaction with FlashAttention & fused kernels:
- FlashAttention incremental decode uses KV pointers; switching pages should update device pointers atomically to the active page region.
- Fused kernels that assume contiguous KV layouts will need an abstraction that can present a contiguous virtual view while physically mapping to paged frames; small memcpy stage may be inevitable for non-resident spans.

Performance microbench plan:
- Set of baselines: current runtime (reference kernels, non-fused), FlashAttention integrated but no fusions, Flash + fusion set 1..n, paged KV with different page sizes.
- Metrics: tokens/sec, p99 latency for single-token decode, GPU memory high-water mark, extra CPU overhead (copy bandwidth), and per-request jitter.
- Hardware vector: A100 80GB, H100 80GB, and representative CPU host (AMD EPYC or Intel Xeon).

Kernel scheduling notes and ideas:
- We currently schedule per-request kernels in a FIFO stream. To maximize CUDA occupancy and hide memcpys for paged KV, consider:
  - A priority-aware scheduler: short decode steps (small-batch low-latency) get higher priority than long batched offline jobs.
  - Cooperative batching windows: hold micro-window (~1–2ms) to accumulate requests for same model/seq-len to form a better batch for fused kernels. This trades tiny added latency for throughput.
  - Overlap: schedule async memcpy of CPU->GPU for paged KV on separate copy stream; use CUDA events to synchronize minimal dependency when kernel needs data.

Correctness and testing strategy:
- Numeric checks: for fp16/bf16, implement unit tests that compare fused kernel outputs to baseline within relative epsilon (1e-3–1e-2 depending on op).
- End-to-end golden tests using small models where we can brute-force reference output across multiple seeds and tokens.
- Stress tests: simulate many concurrent contexts with mixed resident/cold pages to validate eviction/preloading.

Implementation roadmap (proposal):
1) Minimal FlashAttention integration: workspace pool + kernel wrapper + runtime selection policy. (owner: Priya)
2) qkv pack + rotary fusion kernel prototype (owner: Luca)
3) softmax+dropout fusion + test harness (owner: Jordan)
4) paged KV prototype: host <-> device pinned pages + async prefetch + simple LRU (owner: Ethan)
5) scheduler experiment: cooperative batching + priority queueing (owner: TBD)

Experiment tracking and PRs:
- See linked PR #412 for initial FlashAttention wrapper and workspace pool.
- Jira SRV-221 is the project tracking multi-tenant paged KV work.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Page size tuning: default 256 tokens likely ok, but need microbench sweep.
- How to support quantized attention kernels with FlashAttention semantics? Work with quant team on compatible kernels or fallback.
- Decide eviction serialization format: per-kv-block vs per-layer page layout.
- Telemetry: add metrics for "page fault" rate, average page residency time, and per-request page copy time.

Action items (short-term):
- (Ethan) Prototype pinned host page pool + async copy path (2 weeks).
- (Priya) Add workspace pool API and integrate with the initial FlashAttention wrapper (1 week).
- (Luca) Prototype qkv-pack fused kernel on small scale, test for standard GPT dims (1–2 weeks).
- Add microbench harness entries for tokens/sec and p99 latency for ~8 ensemble prompts across lengths [128,512,1024,2048].

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Might be worth exploring device-side page table (NVIDIA MPS or CUDA 12 advanced memory mapping) to avoid memcpy for large pages — research required.
- Keep fallbacks simple: if a fused kernel fails a parity check, runtime should revert to safe slower path and emit an alert to observability.

References & helpful links:
- FlashAttention repo and paper (link in Confluence).
- Internal PRs and issue tracker listed above.

End of notes.
